extracted.intended_audience: CIA Support Directorate staff, agency program managers, and officials responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-44 management improvement programs
extracted.subtask_description: Internal agency implementation of OMB Circular A-44 management improvement requirements, focusing on reports management, information processing systems, records microfilming pilots, and staff-level reporting obligations. The page is an internal memorandum describing tasks, inventories, cost-reduction targets, and pilot project plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reporting (limit to own staff budget and managerial control)
rubrics_metrics.description: In limiting our report to our own Staff budget (which/is primarily personnel costs) and programs under our managerial control, our only input to the Management Improvement Program can be by rendering staff assistance on Agency and Directorate wide programs (i.e. Reports Management Program which is a part of OMB Circular A-44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports submitted under the Management Improvement Program should be confined to the reporting unit's own budget and programs under its managerial control; where primary issues are Directorate- or Agency-wide, the unit's contribution is to provide staff assistance and coordination rather than full program reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information processing systems development and management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Information Processing Branch continues its work in design, testing and implementation of various information processing system areas; at present there are ten major systems under design and these major systems are further subdivided into 41 subsystems or projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria implied: plan and document system designs, conduct testing and implementation phases for major systems and subsystems, develop new concepts and proposals for managing information processing activities, and coordinate proposals in the annual program call. Emphasis on tracking number/scope of systems and subdividing into manageable projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports management: inventory, assessment, and cost-reduction targets
rubrics_metrics.description: SSS is coordinating the Support Directorate reports on cost reduction programs required in transmittal memorandum No. 1 to OMB Circular A-44. The Support Directorate has responsibility for assessing the value and need for regulatory and other centrally prepared management information reports produced by or for offices of the Support Directorate and disseminated throughout the Agency. A reports inventory has been completed identifying 1600 management information reports in the DDS, and with an overall cost of $1,636,000. The cost reduction goal for FY 1972 established by O/PPB for the Support Directorate is a 7.5% reduction of approximately $125,000. Quotas have been assigned to various Support Offices and Support Services Staff will provide assistance in developing a continuing reports management program to meet these goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected actions and evaluation criteria: create a complete reports inventory (count and dollar-cost), assess the value and necessity of each centrally prepared/regulated management information report, set and allocate cost-reduction quotas across offices, and provide staff assistance to develop ongoing reports-management processes to meet percentage/monetary reduction goals. Use inventory data to justify eliminations/consolidations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records microfilming: selection criteria, cost–benefit analysis, and pilot projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey of records for potential microform applications. A recently completed study suggests it may be cost effective to microfilm certain collections of records for the primary purpose of conserving storage space, provided that certain criteria can be met in the collection of files to microfilm. We are now undertaking a detailed cost benefit analysis of a few carefully selected collections of records... We expect to mount two or three pilot filming projects within the next six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and evaluation criteria: identify record collections that meet pre-established criteria for microfilming, perform detailed cost–benefit analyses considering primary purposes (e.g., storage-space relief vs. other objectives), review feasibility and broader system implications with relevant divisions (e.g., Printing Services), and pilot 2–3 projects to validate approaches before wider implementation.
